provenance.notes: Fixtures recombine syntax shapes already represented by repository tests; they contain no copied article or book prose.

expectations.note: Canonical blog writes retain RIN_MARKDOWN_SOURCE and optional file metadata; the legacy browser HTML marker is stripped.
Do not revive RIN_MARKDOWN as the canonical article result slot; task 6.2 adds explicit Renderer provenance.
Headings, paragraphs, emphasis, code, lists and blockquotes move to unified standards behavior.
Retain aligned tables; malformed one-dash separators remain a compatibility fixture, not GFM syntax.
Preserve reader-visible autolinks under the final URL policy.
Milkdown authors the syntax but the legacy browser converter leaves markers literal; remark-gfm becomes canonical.
Milkdown authors the syntax but the legacy browser converter does not emit del; remark-gfm becomes canonical.
Keep repeated references, stable IDs/backrefs and reader scroll semantics through an AST plugin.
Generate collision-safe IDs before final links and TOC are built; do not depend on reader DOM mutation.
The legacy excerpt recognizes alert markers but legacy HTML is literal; task 5.3 must select and validate named schemas.
The separate Go regex parser remains readable until repository import routes through the Renderer.
Preserve exact TeX and display mode for the shared MathJax contract; do not carry source-rewriting heuristics forward.
Keep normalized language plus original info/fence metadata for the Shiki work unit and diagnostics.
Existing stored/source-only content remains readable, but newly published Markdown uses shared MathJax output.
Keep as rollout fallback; final server-highlighted blocks must not be highlighted twice.
Retain explicit title/meaningful-alt captions and generated-alt suppression as typed figure semantics.
Resolve project-relative links and enforce the shared URL policy with diagnostics.
The browser helper historically accepts data:image; shared final-output policy rejects it for new publication.
Existing generated diagram image URLs remain readable and editable through their source endpoint.
Old rin-quiver comments are ignored/stripped; do not make hidden HTML comments the new source contract.
Only allowlisted directive types/options may create RinDiagramUnit work.
Reader text-node recovery is a rollout fallback; canonical Markdown must create a typed unit or diagnostic.
A standalone br line is the only proven raw-HTML compatibility shape; prefer a documented break transform.
Scripts, event handlers, iframes and arbitrary raw HTML are disabled for canonical publication.
Keep existing files/toc/pages JSON readable; new Renderer results gain separate provenance and versioning.
Preserve file/page identity, level 2/3 hierarchy and deterministic paths for incremental compilation.
